title: Quarterly Review: Cautious Investors Tap the Brakes | Dimensional
gist: Dimensional's Q3 2026 review: US stocks stalled after AI-led record highs (S&P +2.3%), the Fed unanimously hiked to 3.75-4% for the first time since 2023 with headline CPI at 3.4%, and the 10-year hit 5.29% (highest since 2002), while EM (+23.4% YTD) was driven by Taiwan/Korea AI chipmakers. Dimensional argues the equity premium is historically unrelated to rate levels and that $40T US debt is priced in, so investors should not shift stock-bond allocations.

themes.theme: US equities stall after AI-led highs

insights.speaker: Dimensional Fund Advisors
insights.so_what: The multi-year US equity engine is decelerating, with gains increasingly concentrated and fragile.
insights.quote: The S&P 500 rose 2.3%, and the tech-heavy Nasdaq added 2.6% as of September 30.

insights.speaker: Dimensional Fund Advisors
insights.so_what: Rates, geopolitics and AI-sentiment are the three live risk drivers for equity multiples.
insights.quote: The slowdown came as tensions continued in the Middle East, scrutiny increased about the pace of AI development, and bond yields rose around the world.

insights.claim: Emerging markets fell 0.4% in Q3 2026 but were up 23.4% year-to-date, nearly double developed markets' gains; MSCI ACWI rose 1.6% and developed ex-US 0.9% in the quarter.

insights.so_what: EM has been the 2026 outperformer, challenging US-centric allocations.

insights.claim: Taiwan and South Korea have vaulted into the world's 10 largest stock markets in 2026, driven largely by AI-chip suppliers TSMC, Samsung and SK Hynix, which account for more than half of EM gains per a cited report.

insights.so_what: EM returns are now effectively an AI-semiconductor trade, concentrating EM risk in a few chipmakers.

insights.claim: Dimensional argues that outperformance can emerge anywhere, so broadly diversified global portfolios are best positioned to capture returns wherever they appear, as with Taiwan and Korea in 2026.

insights.so_what: Supports global diversification over home-bias or concentrated bets.

insights.claim: The Fed unanimously raised the fed funds rate to 3.75%-4.00% in September 2026, its first hike since July 2023, amid persistently high inflation.
insights.speaker: Dimensional Fund Advisors
insights.so_what: Policy has pivoted back to tightening, a regime shift for rate-sensitive assets.
insights.quote: The vote in favor of a rate hike, which was the first since July 2023, was unanimous, unlike some other recent Fed decisions.
insights.locator: A Unified Fed Lifts the Level

insights.claim: US headline CPI inflation was 3.4% year-over-year in August 2026 while core CPI was 2.4%, implying food and energy (amid an oil spike) were the main inflation drivers.
insights.speaker: Dimensional Fund Advisors
insights.so_what: An energy-driven headline gap means the Fed is reacting to supply shocks, not just core demand.
insights.quote: Headline inflation remained elevated at 3.4% in August, while core inflation, which excludes more volatile food and energy items, rose 2.4% from a year ago.
insights.locator: A Unified Fed Lifts the Level

insights.claim: The US 10-year Treasury yield rose to 5.29% by September 30, 2026, its highest since 2002, as Treasuries fell 3.0%, the Bloomberg US Aggregate fell 3.5% and the Global Aggregate (USD-hedged) fell 2.5% in Q3.
insights.speaker: Dimensional Fund Advisors
insights.so_what: Bond losses are significant and long-end yields at multi-decade highs reprice all assets.
insights.quote: US Treasuries fell 3.0%, sending the yield on the benchmark 10-year Treasury up to 5.29% as of September 30.
insights.locator: A Unified Fed Lifts the Level

themes.theme: Equity premium independent of rate level

insights.claim: Because stock discount rates incorporate current interest rates, higher bond yields should, all else equal, lead to higher expected stock returns, so the equity premium need not shrink when rates rise.
insights.speaker: Dimensional Fund Advisors
insights.so_what: Counters the popular 'TINA is dead, rotate to bonds' argument at 5%+ yields.
insights.quote: All else equal, higher bond yields should lead to higher expected stock returns.
insights.locator: With yields at their highest levels

insights.claim: From 1927-2025, the US equity premium averaged about 9.9% in years starting with below-median one-month T-bill rates versus 8.1% in above-median years, a difference that is not statistically reliable.
insights.speaker: Dimensional Fund Advisors
insights.so_what: Historical evidence shows rate levels don't predict stock-over-bill excess returns.
insights.quote: In years when the one-month US Treasury bill rate was below its historical median, the average equity premium was about 9.9% versus 8.1% in above-median-rate years
insights.locator: Exhibit 1 Stocks Shrug?

insights.claim: Dimensional advises investors to be cautious about shifting their stock-bond mix in response to high current yields, since excess stock returns over bills appear similar regardless of rate levels.
insights.speaker: Dimensional Fund Advisors
insights.so_what: Argues against tactical de-risking into fixed income despite multi-decade-high yields.
insights.quote: investors should be cautious changing their stock-bond mix based on current yields

insights.claim: US government debt topped $40 trillion in summer 2026, yet US sovereign CDS spreads have stayed roughly flat for three years apart from a brief April 2025 spike, suggesting no market-perceived deterioration in credit risk.
insights.speaker: Dimensional Fund Advisors
insights.so_what: Debt-doom narratives are not reflected in default-insurance pricing.
insights.quote: For the past three years, the CDS rate has been around the same level, apart from a brief spike in April 2025.

insights.claim: Dimensional argues market prices already embed expectations about government debt levels, so investors should not change asset allocation in response to the $40 trillion debt milestone.
insights.speaker: Dimensional Fund Advisors
insights.so_what: Discourages fiscal-fear-driven portfolio shifts.
insights.quote: Investors may be better off sticking with their plan and not changing their asset allocation in response to a notable, if not shocking, milestone.
